item.title: Business Context
item.description:
What are Clinical Guidelines?

Clinical guidelines are evidence-based recommendations that help clinicians make decisions about patient care in specific clinical circumstances. They are produced by national bodies (e.g., NICE in England/Wales), professional societies, and individual healthcare organisations.

The Challenge

Healthcare professionals face significant challenges when navigating clinical guidelines:

  • Layered complexity: Guidelines exist at multiple levels - national (NICE, SIGN, BNF), regional (NHS Trust/ICB), and local (formulary, commercial agreements). A single clinical question may require consulting guidance from several sources.
  • Volume: NICE alone publishes over 2,000 guidelines, quality standards, and technology appraisals. Each NHS Trust adds local policies on top.
  • Geographic variation: Clinical pathways vary by region. The same condition may be managed differently depending on local funding decisions, available services, and formulary restrictions.
  • Time pressure: Clinicians need answers at the point of care, often during consultations, with limited time to search across multiple sources.
  • Currency: Guidelines are regularly updated. Keeping track of changes across multiple sources is a significant administrative burden.

Current processes rely on clinicians manually searching guideline databases, reading lengthy PDF documents, and cross-referencing multiple sources.

Our Solution

AWS ClinicalCompass addresses these challenges through:

Agentic guideline navigation

An AI agent that understands the structure and hierarchy of clinical guidelines, retrieving from the relevant sources based on the clinical question.

Multi-source aggregation

Retrieves and reasons across national guidelines, local trust policies, and formulary data to provide a unified, contextualised answer.

Evidence-based citations

Every response includes citations to source documents, enabling clinicians to verify recommendations and maintain clinical accountability.

Natural language interaction

Clinicians can ask questions in plain clinical language rather than constructing keyword searches across multiple databases.

Human-in-the-loop design

ClinicalCompass assists clinical decision-making - it does not replace it. All outputs are clearly presented as guideline summaries requiring clinical judgement.

Benefits

  • Time savings: Reduces the effort of searching across multiple guideline databases to a single natural language query.
  • Consistency: Ensures clinicians access the most current, locally-relevant guidance regardless of which source it originates from.
  • Completeness: Surfaces all relevant layers of guidance (national, regional, local) rather than relying on a single source.
  • Workforce productivity: Frees clinical time for direct patient care rather than administrative searching.

Getting Started

Ready to deploy ClinicalCompass in your environment? Follow our installation guide to get started.

item.title: How It Works
item.description:
Overview

AWS ClinicalCompass uses an agentic AI architecture to process clinical queries through multiple stages: understanding the clinical context, retrieving relevant guidelines from multiple sources, resolving conflicts between them, and presenting a cited response.

Query Processing

  1. Patient and guideline selection - The clinician selects a patient from the Patient Selector (populated from DynamoDB via REST API) and optionally filters guideline sources via the Guideline Selector.

  2. Clinical context understanding - The agent interprets the clinical question, identifying the condition, patient context, and type of guidance needed (diagnostic, treatment, referral, prescribing).

  3. Source identification - Based on the query and selected guidelines, the agent determines which knowledge bases are relevant (e.g., NICE for national guidance, local trust formulary for prescribing decisions).

  4. Parallel retrieval - Three specialised agents execute simultaneously: Patient Context Agent queries EHR data, Global Guidelines Agent consults international sources, Local Regulatory Agent checks jurisdiction-specific protocols.

  5. Conflict detection and resolution - The supervisor identifies disagreements between sources and applies precedence rules (local > national > international) to resolve them.

  6. Response generation - The supervisor produces a structured response with clear citations, confidence indicators, safety alerts, alternatives ranked by safety profile, and links to source documents.

Key Features

Guideline hierarchy awareness

ClinicalCompass understands that clinical guidelines operate in layers. National guidance provides the baseline, but local trust policies, formulary decisions, and regional pathways may modify recommendations. The system surfaces all relevant layers.

Conflict resolution

When guidelines from different sources provide different recommendations, ClinicalCompass identifies the conflict and presents both positions with context on which takes precedence in the local setting.

Citation and traceability

Every statement in a response links back to a specific section of a source document. Clinicians can click through to read the full guideline context.

item.title: Architecture
item.description:
AWS ClinicalCompass is built on a serverless architecture using AWS managed services.

System Overview

The system has three major layers: a real-time query path (WebSocket), a REST API for structured data, and data ingestion pipelines that feed the knowledge bases.

Real-Time Query Path

The primary interaction path for clinicians uses WebSocket for streaming responses:

  1. CloudFront serves the static frontend from S3 (OAC-secured)
  2. WebSocket API Gateway handles real-time bidirectional communication
  3. 6 Lambda handlers manage connection lifecycle and query routing
  4. AgentCore Runtime hosts the multi-agent system that processes clinical queries

REST API

An HTTP API Gateway provides structured data endpoints for the frontend UI:

Endpoint Purpose
GET /patients List patients for the Patient Selector dropdown
GET /patients/{id} Retrieve specific patient context
GET /guidelines List available guideline sources for the Guideline Selector

These endpoints read directly from DynamoDB (patient-index and guideline-registry tables), populated by the ingestion pipelines.

AI Processing Engine

The agentic system runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore:

  • Foundation model: Claude Sonnet via Amazon Bedrock
  • Supervisor Agent orchestrates three specialised agents in parallel
  • AgentCore Memory (STM) maintains session context for multi-turn conversations
  • Decision traces stored for audit compliance

See Agents for detailed agent architecture.

Knowledge Base Layer

Three Bedrock Knowledge Bases provide semantic retrieval:

Knowledge Base Content Agent
EHR Patient demographics, labs, medications, allergies Patient Context Agent
Guidelines ACR, ESUR, NICE, WHO clinical guidelines Global Guidelines Agent
Regulatory HAS France, NHS local trust protocols, SOPs Local Regulatory Agent

All KBs use:

  • Embedding: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
  • Chunking: 512 tokens, 20% overlap
  • Vector store: OpenSearch Serverless

Data Ingestion Pipelines

Three separate ingestion paths feed the knowledge bases and DynamoDB:

Patient (EHR) Pipeline 

S3 (ehr-data) → Lambda (EHR Ingestion) → HealthLake (FHIR R4) + DynamoDB (patient-index) + KB sync
  • Triggered by S3 upload events
  • Transforms patient JSON to FHIR R4 format and stores in AWS HealthLake
  • Computes section hashes for differential detection (only changed sections re-processed)
  • Stores structured records in DynamoDB for direct lookups (UI Patient Selector)
  • Syncs to EHR Knowledge Base for RAG retrieval (semantic search by agents)

Guidelines Pipeline 

S3 (guidelines) → Lambda (Guideline Ingestion) → DynamoDB (guideline-registry) + KB sync
  • Triggered by S3 upload events
  • Stores lightweight metadata in DynamoDB (source name, status) for the UI dropdown
  • Full content goes to the Guidelines Knowledge Base for RAG

Regulatory Pipeline 

S3 (local-regulatory) → KB ingestion job (direct sync)
  • No Lambda intermediary — documents sync directly to the Regulatory KB
  • Always consulted by the Local Regulatory Agent (no user selection needed)

Frontend

A vanilla JavaScript application served via CloudFront, using the AG-UI protocol for real-time streaming of agent events to the browser:

  • Patient Selector — dropdown populated from DynamoDB via HTTP API
  • Guideline Selector — choose which guideline sources to consult
  • Citation Panel — click-through links to source documents
  • Decision Trail — expandable reasoning trace with conflict resolution details

Security and Compliance

  • Authentication: Amazon Cognito (USER_PASSWORD_AUTH + USER_SRP_AUTH)
  • Frontend hosting: CloudFront with Origin Access Control (OAC) to S3
  • Data encryption: At rest (S3 SSE, DynamoDB encryption, OpenSearch encryption) and in transit (TLS)
  • Network: All service-to-service communication via AWS internal endpoints
  • Observability: ADOT tracing with clinical decision audit trail

Infrastructure as Code

The entire stack is deployed via AWS CDK (TypeScript):

  • DynamoDB tables (connections, patient-index, guideline-registry)
  • 10 Lambda functions (WebSocket handlers, ingestion, API, keep-alive)
  • WebSocket + HTTP API Gateways
  • S3 buckets (frontend, EHR data, guidelines, regulatory, KB data x3)
  • CloudFront distribution + OAC
  • OpenSearch Serverless collections
  • AWS HealthLake FHIR datastore (patient data in FHIR R4 format)
  • Cognito User Pool
  • SSM Parameter Store (resource IDs, ARNs, endpoints)
  • CloudWatch Events (AgentCore keep-alive every 5 min)

item.title: Installation
item.description:
Deploy ClinicalCompass in your AWS account. The system uses AWS CDK for infrastructure provisioning and a post-deploy script for runtime configuration.

Prerequisites

  • AWS CLI v2, configured (aws configure). Use a recent version that includes the AgentCore commands: aws bedrock-agentcore-control help must work
  • Node.js 18+ and npm
  • Python 3.10+ (3.12 recommended)
  • Docker running, with buildx (Docker Desktop includes it; with Colima, brew install docker-buildx and link it into ~/.docker/cli-plugins/). AgentCore Runtime only runs linux/arm64 images; on an x86 Linux machine or CI runner, enable arm64 emulation once: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
  • AWS CDK: npm install -g aws-cdk
  • Access to Amazon Bedrock foundation models (Claude Sonnet)
# Install Python dependencies
pip install boto3 opensearch-py requests-aws4auth
pip install -r backend/requirements.txt

What Gets Deployed

CDK-managed resources (incremental deploys via cdk diff)

Resource Purpose
Cognito User Pool + App Client Authentication
DynamoDB tables Connections, patient-index, guideline-registry
ECR repository AgentCore container images
IAM roles and policies AgentCore, Lambda, KB access
10 Lambda functions WebSocket handlers, EHR/guideline ingestion, patient/guideline APIs, keep-alive
WebSocket API Gateway Real-time agent communication
HTTP API Gateway REST endpoints (/patients, /guidelines)
S3 buckets Frontend static files, EHR data, guidelines, regulatory, KB data x3
CloudFront + OAC HTTPS frontend hosting from S3
OpenSearch Serverless Vector search for KB retrieval
SSM Parameter Store Resource IDs, ARNs, endpoints, frontend hosting config
CloudWatch Events AgentCore keep-alive (every 5 min)

Script-managed resources (runtime operations)

Script Purpose
post_cdk_setup.py HealthLake, OpenSearch indices, Bedrock KBs, AgentCore Memory, AgentCore Runtime, data upload, config updates
build_and_push_image.py Docker build and push to ECR; refresh existing AgentCore runtime when present
deploy_frontend.py Generate config.js, upload to S3, invalidate CloudFront
cleanup_all.py Full teardown of all resources including orphans

Fresh Deployment

Step 1: Create deployment config 

cp deployment/config.example.py deployment/config.py

Edit deployment/config.py and set:

  • AWS_PROFILE - your named AWS CLI profile
  • AWS_REGION - target region (default: us-east-1)
  • AWS_ACCOUNT_ID - your 12-digit account ID

Step 2: Deploy infrastructure 

cd infra
npm install
npx cdk bootstrap # first time only
npx cdk deploy --require-approval never

Validate: the WebSocket API is up and rejects unauthenticated connections.

npx wscat -c wss://<API_ID>.execute-api.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/production
# Expected: error: Unexpected server response: 401

Step 3: Build and push the agent container

Requires Docker running with buildx (Docker Desktop, or colima start with the buildx plugin). The script always builds a linux/arm64 image, the only architecture AgentCore Runtime runs, and pushes it straight to ECR.

cd ..
python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py

Validate:

aws ecr describe-images --repository-name bedrock-agentcore-clinicalcompass \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1 \
 --query 'imageDetails[0].imageTags'

Common issues:

  • Docker: NOT RUNNING - Start Docker Desktop or run colima start
  • docker buildx is required - Install the buildx plugin (see Prerequisites)
  • Runtime rejects the image as the wrong architecture - Make sure you use this script (it builds linux/arm64), not a plain docker build
  • no basic auth credentials - Remove credsStore from ~/.docker/config.json
  • denied: Your authorization token has expired - Re-run the script (it re-authenticates)

Step 4: Complete setup (HealthLake, KBs, memory, runtime, data) 

python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py

This script:

  1. Creates HealthLake FHIR datastore (if configured)
  2. Creates OpenSearch indices
  3. Creates Bedrock Knowledge Bases
  4. Creates the AgentCore Runtime
  5. Provisions short-term memory
  6. Uploads clinical data to KBs
  7. Updates frontend/config.js and knowledge-bases/knowledge_base_ids.json

Validate:

aws bedrock-agentcore-control list-agent-runtimes \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1 \
 --query 'agentRuntimes[?agentRuntimeName==`clinicalcompass`].{name:agentRuntimeName,status:status}'

Common issues:

  • opensearch-py and requests-aws4auth required - Install them, then re-run with --skip-runtime --skip-memory --skip-config
  • Collection status: CREATING - OpenSearch collections take 2-5 min after CDK deploy. Wait and re-run.
  • Failed to create runtime - Check Docker image was pushed (Step 3) and IAM role exists.

Step 5: Deploy frontend to CloudFront 

python deployment/scripts/deploy_frontend.py

This generates config.js, uploads all frontend files to S3, and invalidates the CloudFront cache. Access via the CloudFront URL printed at the end.

Create a Cognito user with the post-deploy CLI commands in the Authentication section, then log in with that username and password.

For local development, you can also serve the frontend directly after step 4 (which generates config.js):

cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080
# Open http://localhost:8080

Configuration

deployment/config.py holds only your AWS profile, region, and account ID (plus the ECR repository name). Everything else is discovered at run time from the CloudFormation stack outputs and SSM Parameter Store (runtime ARN, memory ID). post_cdk_setup.py also writes:

  • frontend/config.js - Cognito + WebSocket endpoint
  • knowledge-bases/knowledge_base_ids.json - KB identifiers

Config files are gitignored. Only *.example.* templates are committed.

Environment Variables

Variable Description Default
AWS_REGION AWS region us-east-1
BEDROCK_MODEL_ID Bedrock model us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6
BEDROCK_TEMPERATURE Model temperature 0
STM_MEMORY_ID Short-term memory ID Read from SSM
EHR_KB_ID EHR Knowledge Base ID Read from SSM
GUIDELINES_KB_ID Guidelines KB ID Read from SSM
REGULATORY_KB_ID Regulatory KB ID Read from SSM

Authentication

CDK deploys a Cognito User Pool (clinicalcompass-users) with:

  • An app client configured for browser use (no client secret)
  • USER_PASSWORD_AUTH and USER_SRP_AUTH flows enabled

Create login users after deployment with the Cognito admin CLI:

USER_POOL_ID=$(aws cloudformation describe-stacks \
 --stack-name ClinicalCompassStack \
 --region us-east-1 \
 --query "Stacks[0].Outputs[?OutputKey=='CognitoUserPoolId'].OutputValue" \
 --output text)

aws cognito-idp admin-create-user \
 --user-pool-id "$USER_POOL_ID" \
 --username doctor \
 --temporary-password '<STRONG_PASSWORD>' \
 --message-action SUPPRESS \
 --region us-east-1

aws cognito-idp admin-set-user-password \
 --user-pool-id "$USER_POOL_ID" \
 --username doctor \
 --password '<STRONG_PASSWORD>' \
 --permanent \
 --region us-east-1

Choose a password that satisfies the pool policy: at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, and a digit. The frontend authenticates directly via the Cognito InitiateAuth API. Tokens are stored in sessionStorage (cleared on tab close). No external SDK required.

Full Teardown 

python deployment/scripts/cleanup_all.py

S3 buckets and the ECR repository have RETAIN removal policy and won’t be deleted by cdk destroy alone. The cleanup script handles them.

AWS Bedrock may still leave deleted Knowledge Base names behind in DELETE_UNSUCCESSFUL. A subsequent deploy is still safe because post_cdk_setup.py detects those stale names and falls back to a reusable alternate Knowledge Base name when needed.

item.title: Development
item.description:
Day-to-day workflows for modifying agents, updating infrastructure, and managing knowledge bases.

Updating Backend Agents

When you modify code in backend/agents/ or backend/utils/:

python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py

This rebuilds the Docker image and pushes it to ECR. If the clinicalcompass runtime already exists, the script also updates it to the newly pushed image and waits for it to return to READY. During a fresh deploy, no runtime exists yet, so the script just builds and pushes the image.

For faster iteration during development:

bash deployment/scripts/quick_update_agentcore.sh

Updating the Frontend

When you modify frontend HTML, JS, or CSS:

python deployment/scripts/deploy_frontend.py

This regenerates config.js, uploads all files to S3, and invalidates the CloudFront cache. Changes are live in 1-2 minutes.

For local development (after post_cdk_setup.py has generated config.js):

cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080

Updating Lambda Handlers

When you modify code in backend/lambda/websocket/:

cd infra && npx cdk deploy

CDK detects the code change and updates only the affected Lambda functions.

Updating Infrastructure

When you modify the CDK stack (new resources, policy changes):

cd infra
npx cdk diff # preview changes
npx cdk deploy # apply

Updating Knowledge Base Data

When you add or modify clinical data in knowledge-bases/data/:

python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-runtime --skip-memory

This re-uploads data to S3 and triggers a KB sync without touching the runtime or memory configuration.

Project Structure 

aws-clinicalcompanion/
├── backend/
│ ├── agents/ # Multi-agent system
│ │ ├── supervisor_agent.py
│ │ ├── patient_context_agent.py
│ │ ├── global_guidelines_agent.py
│ │ └── local_regulatory_agent.py
│ ├── utils/ # Shared utilities
│ │ ├── session_manager.py
│ │ ├── memory_utils.py
│ │ ├── agui_emitter.py
│ │ ├── metadata_extractor.py
│ │ ├── clinical_observability.py
│ │ └── kb_config.py
│ ├── lambda/websocket/ # 5 Lambda handlers
│ ├── app.py # AgentCore container entry point
│ └── requirements.txt
├── frontend/
│ ├── css/ # Styles (agui, panel, auth)
│ ├── js/ # App logic + auth
│ └── index.html
├── infra/ # CDK infrastructure (TypeScript)
│ ├── lib/
│ └── bin/app.ts
├── knowledge-bases/
│ ├── data/ # Clinical data (EHR, guidelines, regulatory)
│ └── upload_data.py
├── deployment/
│ ├── scripts/ # Deployment and setup scripts
│ └── config.py # Centralised configuration
└── tests/ # Integration and unit tests

Running Tests 

# Backend unit tests (first time: pip install -r backend/requirements-dev.txt)
cd backend && python -m pytest -q

# CDK security assertion tests
cd infra && npx jest

To check a deployed stack end to end, sign in through the CloudFront URL and run a query. The WebSocket API requires a Cognito access token, so unauthenticated tools such as a plain wscat connection are rejected with 401.

Verifying Data Pipelines

EHR Pipeline 

# Upload patient data to trigger ingestion
aws s3 cp knowledge-bases/data/ehr/patient_001_jean_pierre_dubois.json \
 s3://clinicalcompass-ehr-data-<ACCOUNT_ID>/ \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1

# Verify DynamoDB was populated
aws dynamodb scan --table-name clinicalcompass-patient-index \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1 --query 'Count'

# Verify via REST API
curl $(aws ssm get-parameter --name /clinicalcompass/http-api-endpoint \
 --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text)/patients

Guidelines Pipeline 

# Upload a guideline document
aws s3 cp knowledge-bases/data/guidelines/acr_contrast_manual_2024.md \
 s3://clinicalcompass-guidelines-<ACCOUNT_ID>/ \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1

# Check guideline registry
aws dynamodb scan --table-name clinicalcompass-guideline-registry \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1 \
 --query 'Items[*].{source:source_name.S,status:status.S}' --output table

Knowledge Base Vectorisation 

# Test RAG retrieval (proof vectorisation works)
aws bedrock-agent-runtime retrieve \
 --knowledge-base-id <KB_ID> \
 --retrieval-query '{"text": "patient with renal impairment eGFR 32"}' \
 --profile <YOUR_PROFILE> --region us-east-1 \
 --query 'retrievalResults[0].content.text' --output text

Running the Frontend Locally 

cd frontend && python3 -m http.server 8080
# Open http://localhost:8080

Test query (patient 001, Jean-Pierre Dubois):

“68-year-old male with eGFR 32, needs MRI with gadolinium contrast”

CI/CD Integration

The build script supports versioned tags for pipeline use:

# Tag with commit SHA
python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py --tag $CI_COMMIT_SHA

# Build only (no push)
python deployment/scripts/build_and_push_image.py --no-push

Post-CDK Script Options

The post_cdk_setup.py script supports selective execution:

python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py # full setup
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-kb # skip Knowledge Base creation
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-runtime # skip AgentCore Runtime
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-memory # skip Memory creation
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-data # skip KB data upload
python deployment/scripts/post_cdk_setup.py --skip-config # skip config file updates

item.title: Agents
item.description:
ClinicalCompass uses a supervisor pattern where a central orchestrator coordinates three specialised agents that run in parallel. Each agent has a single responsibility and queries its own knowledge base.

Agent Overview 

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Supervisor Agent │
│ (Claude Sonnet - Orchestration & Conflict Resolution) │
└────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
│
├──────────────────┬──────────────────┐
▼ ▼ ▼
┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐
│ Patient Context│ │ Global │ │ Local │
│ Agent │ │ Guidelines │ │ Regulatory │
│ │ │ Agent │ │ Agent │
└────────┬────────┘ └────────┬────────┘ └────────┬────────┘
│ │ │
▼ ▼ ▼
┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐
│ EHR KB │ │ Guidelines KB │ │ Regulatory KB │
└─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘

Supervisor Agent

The orchestrator that manages the entire clinical decision workflow.

Responsibilities:

  1. Parse clinical queries and extract entities (patient demographics, symptoms, intended action)
  2. Coordinate parallel agent execution
  3. Detect conflicts between guideline recommendations
  4. Apply precedence rules (local > national > international)
  5. Generate safety alerts and alternatives
  6. Produce a final recommendation with citations

Tools:

Tool Purpose
detect_conflicts Identifies disagreements between agent responses
apply_precedence_rules Resolves conflicts using local > national > international hierarchy
generate_safety_alerts Analyses contraindications and risks
search_alternatives Finds clinically equivalent safer options
synthesize_recommendation Produces the final cited recommendation

Key behaviours:

  • No intermediate narration between tool calls — only the final recommendation is surfaced
  • Multi-turn conversations supported via session memory
  • Patient data cached within sessions to avoid redundant EHR queries
  • All overridden recommendations documented for audit trail

Patient Context Agent

Retrieves patient-specific data from the EHR knowledge base.

Tool: query_ehr(patient_id, query_context)

Knowledge Base: EHR KB

  • Patient demographics
  • Lab results (eGFR, creatinine, etc.)
  • Current medications
  • Allergies
  • Active conditions

Example query:

query_ehr(
 patient_id="patient_001",
 query_context="kidney function for contrast imaging"
)

Returns: Structured JSON with relevant patient data, labs, medications, allergies, and conditions.

Global Guidelines Agent

Consults international clinical guideline knowledge bases.

Tool: query_guidelines(clinical_scenario, guideline_sources)

Knowledge Base: Global Guidelines KB

  • ACR (American College of Radiology)
  • ESUR (European Society of Urogenital Radiology)
  • NICE (National Institute for Health and Care Excellence)
  • WHO guidelines

Example query:

query_guidelines(
 clinical_scenario="MRI with contrast for patient with reduced kidney function",
 guideline_sources=["ACR", "ESUR", "NICE"]
)

Returns: JSON with source, recommendation text, evidence level, confidence score, and citation.

Local Regulatory Agent

Checks national and local regulatory protocols that may override international guidelines.

Tool: query_regulatory_protocols(clinical_scenario, jurisdiction, protocol_sources)

Knowledge Base: Local Regulatory KB

  • HAS France (Haute Autorité de Santé) protocols
  • NHS local trust policies
  • Regional SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures)
  • Formulary restrictions

Example query:

query_regulatory_protocols(
 clinical_scenario="MRI with contrast for patient with reduced kidney function",
 jurisdiction="France",
 protocol_sources=["HAS"]
)

Returns: JSON with source, requirement text, mandatory/recommended flag, confidence score, and citation.

Conflict Resolution

When agents return contradictory recommendations, the supervisor applies precedence rules:

Local Regulatory > National > International

Example conflict:

  • ACR (International): “Gadolinium contrast can be used with caution for eGFR 30-44”
  • HAS France (Local): “Gadolinium contrast should be avoided for eGFR <45”
  • Resolution: HAS France takes precedence — local protocols are more conservative for patient safety and legal compliance

Rationale for local precedence:

  • Legal compliance in local jurisdiction
  • Patient safety (local protocols are often more conservative)
  • Regulatory requirements that clinicians must follow

Knowledge Bases

All three KBs use the same configuration:

  • Embedding model: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
  • Chunking: 512 tokens, 20% overlap
  • Vector store: OpenSearch Serverless
  • Retrieval: Semantic search via Bedrock Knowledge Bases

Data sources 

knowledge-bases/data/
├── ehr/ # Patient records
├── guidelines/ # International clinical guidelines
└── regulatory/ # Local regulatory protocols

Session Management

  • Multi-turn conversations use session_id for context continuity
  • Patient data is cached in AgentCore short-term memory within a session
  • Follow-up questions reference previous context without re-querying
  • Session timeout: 30 minutes of inactivity

Performance

  • Full multi-agent workflow: 30-40 seconds
  • All three specialised agents execute in parallel
  • Hot storage retrieval (decision traces): <200ms
  • Individual KB query: 2-5 seconds

item.title: Observability
item.description:
ClinicalCompass uses AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) for tracing, with custom clinical spans for healthcare-specific events.

Architecture 

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Supervisor Agent │
│ Custom Clinical Spans via │
│ clinical_observability.py │
└───────────────┬─────────────────┘
│
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry │
│ (Automatic instrumentation) │
└───────────────┬─────────────────┘
│
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Amazon CloudWatch │
│ Logs • Traces • Metrics │
└───────────────┬─────────────────┘
│
▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ GenAI Observability Dashboard │
│ Sessions • Agents • Traces │
└─────────────────────────────────┘

What Gets Instrumented

AgentCore provides automatic observability:

  • All agent invocations are traced
  • Tool calls logged with inputs/outputs
  • Errors and exceptions captured
  • Session context preserved across invocations

Custom clinical spans add healthcare-specific signals:

  • Conflict detection - when guidelines disagree
  • Precedence rule application - how conflicts are resolved
  • Recommendation generation - final clinical output
  • Agent coordination - per-agent timing and success

Enabling Observability

AgentCore (Production)

Observability is configured in .bedrock_agentcore.yaml:

observability:
 enabled: true

Custom clinical spans require an additional environment variable:

# In backend/app.py
import os
os.environ['AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED'] = 'true'

Local Development 

export AGENT_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED=true
export OTEL_PYTHON_DISTRO=aws_distro
export OTEL_PYTHON_CONFIGURATOR=aws_configurator
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
export OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES=service.name=clinical-compass

Viewing Logs

CloudWatch Logs (CLI) 

# View recent application logs
aws logs tail \
 /aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/clinicalcompass-DEFAULT \

GenAI Observability Dashboard

  1. Open CloudWatch Console
  2. Navigate to GenAI Observability → Bedrock AgentCore → Agents
  3. Select clinicalcompass
  4. View sessions, traces, and metrics

CloudWatch Logs Insights Queries

Find all sessions:

fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /session/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 100

Find custom clinical spans:

fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /clinical\./
| sort @timestamp desc

Find errors:

fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /ERROR/ or @message like /Exception/
| sort @timestamp desc

Track a specific session:

fields @timestamp, @message
| filter @message like /<SESSION_ID>/
| sort @timestamp asc

Custom Clinical Spans

The backend/utils/clinical_observability.py module provides span helpers:

from clinical_observability import (
 record_conflict_detection,
 record_precedence_rule_application,
 record_recommendation_generation,
 record_agent_coordination,
 clinical_span,
)

# Conflict detection
record_conflict_detection(session_id, conflicts, patient_id)

# Precedence rule application
record_precedence_rule_application(
 session_id=session_id,
 conflict="Contrast use for eGFR 32",
 chosen_guideline="HAS France",
 overridden_guideline="ACR International",
 rationale="Local regulatory requirements take precedence",
 patient_id=patient_id
)

# Recommendation generation
record_recommendation_generation(session_id, recommendation, patient_id)

# Agent coordination timing
record_agent_coordination(
 session_id=session_id,
 agent_name="patient_context",
 duration_ms=1500,
 success=True,
 patient_id=patient_id
)

# Custom spans
with clinical_span("custom.operation", session_id=session_id) as span:
 span.set_attribute("custom.attribute", "value")

Dual Storage Strategy

Clinical decision traces use two storage tiers:

Tier Technology Latency Retention Use Case
Hot AgentCore Memory <100ms 24-48h UI “View Full Reasoning” button
Cold CloudWatch Logs (OTEL) 5-10s 90 days+ Audit, compliance, forensics

The hot tier stores a structured JSON decision trace written at the end of each recommendation. The cold tier receives complete OTEL spans automatically.

Troubleshooting

Dashboard not showing data

  1. Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search - AWS Console → CloudWatch → Settings → Enable Transaction Search
  2. X-Ray permissions are included in the CDK stack: the AgentCore role can write traces (xray:PutTraceSegments, PutTelemetryRecords, GetSamplingRules, GetSamplingTargets) and bedrock-agentcore metrics. If you still see Failed to export span batch code: 403, check that Transaction Search (step 1) is enabled.
  3. Run a test query and wait 1-2 minutes

Logging scripts 

# AgentCore runtime logs (runtime ID is read from SSM, so it always matches the deployed runtime)
python deployment/scripts/check_agentcore_logs.py --minutes 30

# Lambda logs, e.g. the WebSocket query handler
aws logs tail /aws/lambda/clinicalcompass-ws-query --since 30m --follow --region us-east-1
